where: Section 2, the boxed test and the sentence below it
problem: The two consistent cases are written as 'r = r′ = r < n' and 'r = r′ = r < n'. The chain 'r = r′ = r' is a tautology (r always equals r), so a student reads a condition that says nothing and may not see that the real condition is 'the common rank is less than n'. The notation also repeats the symbol r in two roles: the common value and the name of rank A.
fix: Write the cases as: r < r′ → no solution; r = r′ and r = n → one solution; r = r′ and r < n → n − r free variables, with the note 'here r = rank A = rank [A|b]'.

problem: 'An r×r minor on pivot rows and pivot columns is nonzero' is loose: pivot rows are rows of the echelon form, not necessarily rows of A, so a student may think the nonzero minor is read straight off A without eliminating first.
fix: Say instead: eliminate A to an echelon form, note which rows are the pivot rows (tracking any row swaps) and which are the pivot columns; then the r×r submatrix of A on those row positions and column positions has nonzero determinant, and any (r+1)×(r+1) submatrix of A is singular because its rows are dependent.
